summary: notification-service OOMKills are caused by an unbounded in-memory template cache introduced in deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z). memory_pct ramps linearly ~5.4%/hour starting 2026-03-21T00:10Z (flat ~48% before), reaching ~97% and triggering a restart roughly every 24h (03-21T21:55, 03-22T19:40, 03-23T19:50). request_rate (~140/s), cpu_pct (~25%) and latency_p99 (~110ms) are all flat across the period, ruling out traffic/replay/load and downstream degradation. The reported Kafka maintenance (cfg-2410, retention change at 2026-03-23T18:00Z) postdates memory-onset by ~2 days, and consumer_lag spikes occur only in the same buckets as the restarts (restart catch-up), so Kafka is an effect, not the cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory template cache (dep-5402) leaks memory -> OOMKill
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-5402 introduced a ConcurrentHashMap TemplateCache keyed by template+locale+userSegment with no eviction bound; as renders accumulate unique keys, heap grows ~5.4%/hr until the container is OOMKilled roughly every 24h, causing restarts, brief unavailability (error_rate spikes) and consumer catch-up lag spikes.

causal_chain.claim: cache growth -> linear memory ramp starting 2026-03-21T00:10Z
restart causes brief 5xx and consumer catch-up lag spikes

assumptions: The cache has no size/TTL eviction (not documented in the deploy summary)
render key cardinality grows over time (per userSegment/locale) so entries are effectively never reused/reclaimed

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance/replay causes consumer to choke on messages
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The Kafka retention change cfg-2410 and/or a consumer-group replay floods notification-service, driving memory growth and OOMKills as reported.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Memory ramp began 2026-03-21T00:10Z, ~2 days BEFORE cfg-2410 (2026-03-23T18:00Z). consumer_lag spikes occur only in the same buckets as the restarts (catch-up after restart), not before them, and cpu_pct/request_rate/latency are flat — inconsistent with a message flood.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External email-provider degradation backs up retries
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external email-provider degrades, causing retry buffering and memory growth in notification-service.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: latency_p99_ms is flat (~110ms) and error_rate stays at baseline ~0.2% except during restart buckets; no provider-side telemetry but no signal of dependency degradation. Memory ramp starts exactly at the deploy, not at any provider event.

facts.statement: dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 2026-03-21T00:00Z) added an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache to notification-service.
notification-service memory_pct was flat ~47-49% before 2026-03-21T00:10Z, then ramped steadily to ~92-98%.
memory_pct shows a ~24h sawtooth reaching ~97% before resetting to ~50%.
request_rate (mean 140/s) and cpu_pct (mean 25%) are flat across the window; no traffic/load increase.
consumer_lag spikes (max 17161, 17611, 18137) occur only in the same buckets as the restarts.
Kafka cfg-2410 changed retention at 2026-03-23T18:00Z, ~2 days after memory growth began.
latency_p99_ms remains flat ~110ms; no dependency latency degradation.
error_rate spikes to ~13-14% only in restart buckets vs ~0.2% baseline.
No notification-service deployment occurred before 2026-03-20; dep-5402 is the only code change in-window.

assumptions: The TemplateCache in dep-5402 has no eviction/TTL bound (inferred from the deploy summary; not directly shown in logs since logs were unavailable).
The render key space (template+locale+userSegment) accumulates unique entries over time rather than being small and reused.
The restarts counter reflects OOMKill restarts (consistent with the memory sawtooth reaching ~97%).

timeline.event: Deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) adds in-memory template cache to notification-service.
memory_pct stops being flat (~48%) and begins linear ramp.
First restart (cumulative=1); memory ~97%, consumer_lag spike 17161, error_rate spike.
Kafka cfg-2410 reduces log retention (reported maintenance); postdates leak onset by ~2 days.
Third restart (cumulative=3); consumer_lag spike 18137; reported incident.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back notification-service to the version before dep-5402 (v3.8.0) to stop the leak immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Memory ramp begins exactly at the deploy and the only in-window code change is dep-5402's cache; rollback should halt the sawtooth.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not feasible, bound the TemplateCache (max size / TTL / LRU eviction) via config or hotfix.
recommended_actions.rationale: The cache keyed by template+locale+userSegment grows unbounded; an eviction bound caps heap growth.

recommended_actions.action: Add heap-usage and cache-entry-count alerts and raise the container memory limit pending the fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: Early-warning on the ~5.4%/hr ramp prevents silent OOM cycles.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT pursue a Kafka replay fix for this incident; treat consumer_lag spikes as restart side-effects.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag spikes coincide with restarts and postdate memory onset; Kafka config change postdates onset by 2 days.

recommended_actions.action: Restore log pipeline access (query_logs circuit-open) and review OOM/GC logs to confirm eviction behaviour post-fix.
recommended_actions.rationale: Logs were unavailable during the incident, limiting direct confirmation of the leak.

data_gaps: query_logs for notification-service was unavailable throughout (503 then circuit-open) — no application logs, stack traces, OOM/GC messages, or cache-size instrumentation could be inspected to directly confirm the cache leak or its eviction policy.
email-provider (external) has no telemetry, so dependency-side health could not be verified directly; ruled out only via flat latency/error metrics.
Exact per-restart timestamps are inferred from 8700s metric buckets, so restart times are approximate.
No visibility into the TemplateCache implementation detail (eviction, key cardinality) beyond the deploy change summary.

findings.statement: Deployment dep-5402 for notification-service (v3.8.0, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z) added an in-memory template cache: 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment'.

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct was flat (~47-49%) through 2026-03-20 and until 2026-03-21T00:10Z, then began a steady climb (~54% at 02:35) reaching ~92-98% peaks.
memory_pct shows a repeating sawtooth: ramp to ~97%, drop to ~50%, repeat every ~24h, with max values 97.37, 97.98 and 97.56 on successive days.
restarts counter increments by 1 at ~2026-03-21T21:55Z, ~2026-03-22T19:40Z and ~2026-03-23T19:50Z (cumulative 0->1->2->3), each coinciding with the memory sawtooth resets.
request_rate is flat across the whole window (mean 140.17 req/s, range 115-172), showing no traffic increase coincident with the memory ramp.
cpu_pct is flat (~25%) across the entire window including the memory-ramp period.

consumer_lag is low (~57-65) on 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-21 up to ~17:05Z, then spikes to avg 1890 / max 17161 at 2026-03-21T21:55Z — the same bucket as the first restart — and again ~17611 at 2026-03-22T19:40Z and ~18137 at 2026-03-23T19:50Z.
Kafka config change cfg-2410 reduced log.retention.ms from 604800000 to 259200000 at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z, i.e. ~2 days after memory growth began.
latency_p99_ms is flat (~110ms mean) across the whole window, showing no downstream/dependency latency degradation.
error_rate is ~0.2% baseline but spikes to max 13.78/14.73/13.96 in the buckets containing the restarts (2026-03-21T20:00Z, 03-22T20:00Z, 03-23T16:00Z).
notification-service consumes from a shared kafka queue and calls an external email-provider; email-provider has no telemetry.
query_logs for notification-service failed repeatedly (503) and then circuit-opened (retryable=false), so no log lines were obtainable.
